2. Shu, Pan 论文解读

Abstract: In this paper, we introduce super Weyl groups, their distinguished elements and properties for basicclassical Lie superalgebras. Then we formulate Jantzen filtration for baby Verma modules in graded restrictedmodule categories of basic classical Lie superalgebras over an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic,and obtain a sum formula in the corresponding Grothendieck groups. Consequently, we formulate a stronglinkage principle for such categories.

2.1 Introduction

Recently, the topic on representations of basic classical Lie superalgebras and the corresponding algebraicsupergroups in prime characteristic becomes more and more attractive (cf. [2–4, 24, 28–30, 34, 38–44] etc.).In such topic, it is a key point to understand irreducible modules through standard modules (baby Vermamodules). However, the information on this has been known little. Recall that in the Bernstein-Gelfand-Gelfand categories of complex semisimple Lie algebras, and in (rational) representation categories of mod-ular reductive algebraic groups and of their reductive Lie algebras associated with specific tori of the corre-sponding algebraic groups, some kinds of artfully-constructed filtrations of standard modules, introducedby Jantzen in [15] for complex semisimple Lie algebras, and in [18, 19] for modular reductive algebraicgroups and their Lie algebras, are very powerful tools to understand character formulas of irreducible mod-ules through the ones of standard modules (cf. [13, 15, 17–19] etc.). In this paper, we extend the theory ofJantzen filtration for modular reductive Lie algebras to the super case.

We will focus on restricted representations of a basic classical Lie superalgebra g over k, an algebraicallyclosed field of characteristic . In order to establish a satisfactory theory on characters for restrictedirreducible modules in the modular case, a usual way is to refine the restricted module category modof by introducing ℤ-graded structures. So we will actually work with a graded restricted module category -mod, via an additional T-action for a maximal torus T of an algebraic supergroup G with (see Definition 4.1).

A super Weyl group is introduced here, which is a subgroup of the symmetric group of the set of allBorel subalgebras containing a standard Cartan subalgebra, generated by all real reflections and odd reflec-tions. In our construction of the Jantzen filtration for baby Verma modules in -mod, an importantingredient is to find a distinguished element ŵ of the super Weyl group for (see Theorem 3.10) whichplays a role as important as the longest elements of usual Weyl groups. Another critical ingredient is to construct a series of homomorphisms between graded baby Verma modules, arising from simple odd roots ofdiferent simple root systems varying dependently on the reduced expressions of , and then to analyzeand integrate them. The latter is also a critical dificulty and a critical diference from the ordinary Lie algebracase.

With the above points, we finally obtain a satisfactory filtration and sum formula (see Theorem As a consequence, we can read of a strong linkage principle from the sum formula (see Theorem 7.6 andTheorem 7.2).

One can compare some related results over complex numbers (cf. [31, Chapter 10] and [32, 37]).

2.2 Preliminaries

Throughout the article, the notations of vector spaces (resp. modules, subalgebras) means vector superspaces(resp. super-modules, super-subalgebras). For simplicity, we omit the adjunct word “super”. For a superspace , the homogeneous element v is assumed to have a parity . All vector spaces are definedover k for an algebraically closed field of characteristic

In this section, we will recall some knowledge on basic classical Lie superalgebras along with the correspond-ing algebraic supergroups. We refer the readers to [6, 21, 31] for Lie superalgebras, and to [2, 7, 27, 34] foralgebraic supergroups.
